## Summary

Make **irreversibility** an engine guarantee rather than an authoring
convention: a resource key declared irreversible can never be **granted** by an
option `#extra` (or by any other content path), and the refusal is a hard
authoring error plus a runtime refusal — not a fixture test and a habit.

GDD engine-gap entry **G5** (`docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.3), which
unlocks §2.8 `hull` as the irreversible tension dial (0–5, no recovery within a
run), §2.10 irreversible-loss tension, and §2.8.6 item 6 (`#extra=hull:1` is
legal content today).

## Problem statement

Today the promise "nothing ever grants `hull` back" is enforced by authoring
discipline and one fixture test. The engine has no notion of an irreversible
key: `#extra=hull:1` validates cleanly, resolves cleanly and banks a hull point,
so a single typing mistake silently refunds the dial that the whole tension
model rests on.

## Users

- **Story-line content writer** — wants `npm run storylines:validate` to fail
  when a row grants an irreversible key, with the row, column and key named.
  - "As a writer, when I type `#extra=hull:1` I get a validation error naming
    the row and the key, not a hull refund in play."
- **Game designer** — wants the irreversible set to be a declaration the engine
  enforces, so a re-tune of content cannot quietly restore the dial.
  - "As a designer, I declare `hull` irreversible once and the engine proves no
    content grants it."
- **Engine producer** — wants one declaration, one validation rule and one
  resolution guard, with no per-game re-implementation.
  - "As a producer, I want the rule in `@story-line` once, so a second game with
    an irreversible key gets the same guarantee for free."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A positive `#extra` (an `extraEffect` gain) on a key declared irreversible is
  refused at authoring time: `validateStorylineOptions` (and through it
  `validateContent` / `npm run storylines:validate`) reports a hard issue with a
  stable code (`irreversible-grant`, on the existing `ContentIssueCode` union or
  as a `reason` under an existing code) naming the card id, the CSV row, the
  `options` column and the offending key, and validation fails.
- A **cost** on an irreversible key (`#cost=hull:1`) still validates and still
  resolves: an irreversible key may be spent, never granted.
- At resolution time a grant to a declared irreversible key is refused — the key
  is not applied, and the refusal is reported once in the activity log naming
  the key — while the rest of the option still resolves (cost paid, effect
  applied, successor pushed).
- A fixture CSV row that grants a declared irreversible key exists and a unit
  test asserts the `irreversible-grant` diagnostic for it end-to-end through
  `storylines:validate`, including the reported row and column.
- With **no** irreversible key declared, behaviour is byte-identical to today
  (the default `coins` / `reputation` pair declares none), so every existing
  story-line suite and fixture stays green without edits.
- The structural recovery path is untouched: the reset ending still restarts the
  run at the declared start bag, and the existing routing/reset tests
  (`episode-runner-routing.test.ts`, `episode-runner-loss-ledger.test.ts`) stay
  green — the guard refuses *content grants*, never a structural reset.
- One authoritative declaration: the manifest's `resources.irreversible`, the
  content-adapter declaration and the engine projection cannot drift silently —
  either the wiring is derived from a single source or a mismatch is reported,
  and the chosen direction is documented in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`.
- Documentation: `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (the contract + the new
  diagnostic) and the GDD (`§2.8.3`, `§2.8.6` item 6, `§2.8.7`, `§6.6`
  disposition → delivered) are updated, and
  `tests/story-line/content/gdd-engine-gap-backlog.test.ts` passes with the
  updated disposition record.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A key declared irreversible can no longer be refilled by content, so a writer
sees a validation error instead of a silent rule-breaking grant — the hull dial
stays a real, unrefundable cost of play.

## Constraints

- **`#extra` is a gain by definition** — `validateStorylineOptions` already
  rejects a negative `extraEffect`, so "grant" means any non-zero positive
  `extraEffect` on an irreversible key. No sign-ambiguous encoding to handle.
- **The two seams are different.** `resolveStorylineOption` is manifest-free
  (it takes only state + adapter + card + option), so the runtime guard needs
  the irreversible set declared at the engine seam and fed from the manifest at
  wiring time. The CSV content validator never sees a manifest, so authoring
  validation needs its own declaration (content-adapter data and/or a CLI flag).
- **Do not change `applyResourceDelta` arithmetic.** Bounds/clamping are G4
  (`CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`, in progress) on the same projection seam; the G5
  refusal belongs upstream of the apply, at delta *selection*.
- **Backward compatible by construction:** no irreversible declaration ⇒
  unchanged behaviour and unchanged diagnostics.
- **Re-use the existing undeclared-key reporting channel** (`ignored` in
  `selectDeclaredDelta` → an activity-log line) rather than adding a new adapter
  member, so no game needs to implement anything new.
- **Scope discipline:** bounds/clamping (G4), surfaced affordability (G7),
  compound conditions (G6) and the resource HUD (G8) stay out — file or link
  separate items instead of widening this one.

## Existing state (evidence at this commit)

- `src/story-line/validate.ts::validateStorylineOptions` (line ~147) validates
  `cost` (> 0), `extraEffect` (finite, **non-negative**) and condition fields
  against the declared set, emitting `unknown-resource-key` /
  `unknown-condition-field`. There is no direction rule.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — `ContentIssueCode` union (line ~56) has
  no direction code; the `reason` field carries the sub-code. The declared set is
  `card.resourceKeys` when present, else `DEFAULT_RESOURCE_KEYS` (line ~373),
  and option metadata is validated through `validateStorylineOptions` (~377).
- `src/story-line/resources.ts::selectDeclaredDelta(source, sign, declared)`
  (line ~292) filters **undeclared** keys into `ignored`; a declared key is
  forwarded with whatever sign it was given. `createResourceProjection(fields)`
  (line ~361) treats the field map as the declared set and has no
  irreversibility parameter.
- `src/story-line/resolve.ts::applyDeclaredDelta` (line ~138) forwards
  `extraEffect` with sign `+1` and logs undeclared keys as
  `Extra effect ignored undeclared resource(s): …`.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — `resources.irreversible` is
  manifest data and the rules **already exist and are delivered** (G2, epic
  `CG-0MWR0BFMW003856N`): `resource-set-mismatch` with reason
  `irreversible-not-declared` (line ~908) and `loss-not-irreversible`
  (line ~1120). The item's original "the manifest validator does not exist"
  note is stale.
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` reads `manifest.resources.irreversible`
  (line ~819) for the loss-ledger diff window; loss rules apply `-amount` only
  (~876), so the beat sheet cannot grant a key — only content `#extra` can.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` — `LONG_ERASURE_RESOURCES` (line
  ~116, `hull` first) and `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` (hull starts at 5); no
  irreversibility declaration reaches the engine today.
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts::LONG_ERASURE_CONTENT_ADAPTER` (line ~108)
  declares columns/fields only; `ContentAdapter` (`content/types.ts` ~159) has no
  resource or irreversibility member.
- Existing guards this item replaces: `tests/story-line/content/gdd-resource-model.test.ts`
  (asserts zero `extraEffect.hull` by scanning authored content),
  `tests/fixtures/story-line/gdd-resource-trades.csv`, and the GDD prose in
  §2.8.3 / §2.8.6 / §2.8.7.

## Desired change

1. A declarative irreversible set carried at the engine seam, with the declared
   set (single source, or a reported mismatch — see Design notes).
2. One authoring-time validation rule that refuses a positive `#extra` on an
   irreversible key, reported with card id, CSV row, column and key so a writer
   can act on it.
3. One resolution-time guard that refuses the same grant, logs the refusal once
   and leaves the rest of the resolution intact.
4. The Gym long-erasure game declaring `hull` irreversible, so the guarantee is
   exercised by real content rather than only by a unit fixture.
5. Docs updated: the story-line engine contract, the GDD gap record (G5 →
   delivered) and the structural backlog test.

## Design notes (plan resolves the seam)

- **Runtime declaration seam**
  - (a) `createResourceProjection(fields, { irreversible })`, exposing
    `irreversible` on `StorylineResourceProjection` — mirrors how the declared
    set is already carried. **Recommended:** the projection *is* the
    declaration today, so irreversibility belongs beside it.
  - (b) A new `StorylineEngineAdapter.irreversibleResources` member — a second
    parallel seam that can drift from `resources`.
  - (c) Manifest-only, enforced in `episode-runner.ts` — leaves the
    manifest-free `resolveStorylineOption` path unguarded, so it fails the
    promise.
- **Authoring declaration seam**
  - (a) `ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources?` (per-game data, already the
    natural home for `long-erasure`), optionally overridden by a
    `storylines:validate --irreversible <key>` flag. **Recommended:** keeps the
    manifest-free validator honest and needs no new CLI surface for the shipped
    adapters.
  - (b) CLI flag only — every invocation must remember it; a forgotten flag
    silently disables the guarantee.
  - (c) Cross-check the CSV `#extra` cells from the manifest validator — one
    declaration source, but the manifest validator would have to read raw CSV
    option encodings, a much larger surface.
- **Refusal reporting** re-uses the existing `ignored` channel shape at
  resolution (`Extra effect refused: hull is irreversible.`), so no new adapter
  member is required.

## Key Files

- `src/story-line/validate.ts` — new direction rule in `validateStorylineOptions`
  and an `irreversible` config field.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — irreversible-aware `selectDeclaredDelta`; the
  projection option carrying the irreversible set.
- `src/story-line/resolve.ts` — thread the irreversible set into
  `applyDeclaredDelta` and log the refusal.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — the `irreversible-grant` issue code (or
  reason) and the declaration plumbing.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` / `adapters.ts` — `ContentAdapter`
  irreversibility declaration (per Design notes (a)).
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — pass the declaration through, and the
  optional `--irreversible` override.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` — declare `hull` irreversible and
  wire the projection.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — the contract, the diagnostic table row and
  the wiring direction.
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — §2.8.3, §2.8.6 item 6, §2.8.7 and §6.6
  disposition updated to delivered.
- `tests/story-line/validate.test.ts`, `tests/story-line/resource-semantics.test.ts`,
  `tests/story-line/resource-declaration.test.ts`,
  `tests/story-line/content/gdd-resource-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/story-line/content/gdd-engine-gap-backlog.test.ts`, plus a new
  `tests/story-line/irreversible-policy.test.ts` for the end-to-end rule.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Declaration drift** between the manifest's `resources.irreversible`, the
  content adapter and the engine projection. Mitigation: derive from one source
  where possible, otherwise report a mismatch; document which side is
  authoritative. (AC covering this.)
- **Scope creep into G4** (same `applyResourceDelta` seam, in progress as
  `CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`). Mitigation: refuse at selection, never in the apply
  arithmetic; coordinate if both land in the same module in one window.
- **Silently breaking legitimate content** that already grants a key a game now
  declares irreversible. Mitigation: no declaration ⇒ unchanged; audit the Gym
  long-erasure content before declaring `hull` (the fixture test says there is
  currently no `extraEffect.hull`).
- **Reset/structural recovery mistaken for a grant.** The reset ending restarts
  the run at the declared start bag rather than applying a delta; the guard must
  not block it. Mitigation: the AC pins the routing/loss-ledger tests.
- **Assumption (documented):** the refusal is non-fatal at resolution (like the
  existing undeclared-key case) and hard-fatal at authoring time, per the GDD's
  "reject at authoring time … refuse, log at resolution".
- **Assumption (documented):** the diagnostic is additive — a new code on the
  existing union (or a new `reason` under an existing code) — so downstream
  tooling that switches on `code` keeps compiling.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — GDD engine-gap backlog (source; completed).
- `CG-0MWR0BHH9002OQUZ` — this item (G5).
- `CG-0MWR0BFMW003856N` — G2, episode manifest schema + validator (delivered):
  owns `resources.irreversible` and the `loss-not-irreversible` rule.
- `CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X` — G4, resource bounds/spill/clamped loss (in progress):
  same projection seam, different concern — coordination risk.
- `CG-0MWR0BG9H007AFNU` — G3, scene-space guard over the episode manifest
  (in progress): the reachability proof that consumes the same manifest block.
- `CG-0MWNHZ67Q005BWE0` / `CG-0MWQZJEXQ002G3KE` — declared resource set in the
  story-line engine and the per-file declaration seam (the declared-set
  precedent this item extends to a direction rule).
- `CG-0MWT4UU66003ANZ8` — episode runner loss ledger: the consumer of
  `resources.irreversible` at runtime.
- Docs: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` (§2.8, §2.8.3, §2.8.6 item 6,
  §2.8.7, §6.3 G5, §6.6), `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (validation and
  resource contracts).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Where should the irreversible set live at runtime — the projection, a
  new adapter member, or the manifest only?**
  Answer (intake, from evidence): not settled by the repo; recorded as Design
  notes with a recommendation (projection option + manifest-fed wiring) for plan
  to confirm. Research: inspected `src/story-line/resources.ts`
  (`createResourceProjection` has no irreversibility parameter),
  `src/story-line/resolve.ts` (`resolveStorylineOption` is manifest-free) and
  `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (the only manifest-aware layer). Non-blocking
  — either choice satisfies the acceptance criteria.
- **Q: How does the CSV content validator learn the irreversible keys, given it
  never reads a manifest?**
  Answer (intake, from evidence): recorded as Design notes with a recommendation
  (`ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources`, optionally overridden by a
  `storylines:validate` flag). Research: inspected
  `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` (already selects a per-game adapter via
  `--game long-erasure`) and `src/story-line/content/types.ts`
  (`ContentAdapter` has no resource member). Non-blocking.
- **Q: Should a refused grant abort resolution or be a non-fatal refusal?**
  Answer: the GDD (§2.8.6 item 6 and G5's proposed shape) states "reject a
  positive delta … at authoring time … and at resolution time (refuse, log)", so
  resolution is a refusal plus a log line, matching the existing
  undeclared-key behaviour. Source: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.3 G5,
  §2.8.6. Resolved, no follow-up.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MWSJYLZ3005C2V1** – Episode manifest resource model rules and declared start/bounds (completed)
- **CG-0MWSJYPAX002O63N** – Episode manifest semantic and numeric rules (completed)

## Summary

Retire the legacy **`act` / `clockCost` CSV columns** now that act membership and pacing are beat-sheet data: remove them from the Gym content adapter, migrate the remaining rows, and add the migration check that refuses a disagreeing manifest/CSV pair while both exist.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.1 composition contract (act membership is `scene.id`; pacing is `beat.clockCost` in the manifest).
- §2.9 "the two retired columns" and §2.4 `clock-cost-mismatch` (migration-only rule).
- §2.9.7 friction 5 (act/clock as generic `--field` writes).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` declares `act` and `clockCost` as Gym game columns and lists both in `editableColumns` (with defaults `I` / `1`), so authors can still write beat-sheet data into the wrong place.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` reads `clockCost` per beat for its pressure clock.
- The migration check (`clock-cost-mismatch`) only becomes possible once the manifest validator exists (G2), so this entry depends on it.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the adapter column declaration/removal itself in `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` plus the `missing-column` diagnostic in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts`.
- Band is small because it is a content-format change with a migration, not new machinery; the validator rule is the only new logic.

## Proposed shape

- Migrate the spike's `act` / `clockCost` values into the episode manifest (Appendix A carries the same data).
- Remove both columns from the adapter and `editableColumns`; the spike's rule module reads the manifest instead.
- While both forms exist, the manifest validator rejects a disagreeing pair (`clock-cost-mismatch`); once removed, the content validator refuses the columns as unknown.
- Unit tests: CSV with the retired column fails loudly; manifest/CSV agreement passes; mismatch fails.

## Summary

Add **keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order**: number/arrow navigation of the option list with Enter/Space activation, focus traversal inside an open overlay, and Escape closing only the topmost modal — so the keyboard path in the GDD's accessibility contract is real rather than aspirational.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.4 keyboard and touch input paths.
- §3.6 B7; §3.8 (the keyboard path is untestable until this lands).
- §3.2 overlay behaviour (exactly one modal live, Escape closes the topmost).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- Only the panels' own toggle keys are bound: `HelpPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `FORWARD_SLASH` = `?`) and `SettingsPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `Escape`) register their own `keydown` listeners (`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`).
- `getEndTurnKeybind()` / `setEndTurnKeybind()` in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` bind exactly one game action.
- No choice-list navigator, focus-trap or focus-order helper is exported from `src/ui/index.ts`.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedents are the `keydown` listener lifecycle in `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` (register/off on destroy) and `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` (one live modal, ordered open/close) + `src/ui/Overlay.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one navigator helper plus focus handling on the existing overlay primitives.

## Proposed shape

- `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, { count, onChoose, keys? })` — `1`-`6` and arrows + Enter/Space, disabled while a modal is open.
- `attachOverlayFocus(scene, overlayObjects, { onEscape })` — traversal order, activation, Escape topmost-only.
- Both return a disposer, and both respect reduced motion/no-ops in headless tests.
- Unit tests: index keys select the right option; arrow wrap; Escape closes only the topmost; disposer removes listeners.

## Summary

Add a **shared verbosity preference** (Full / Concise) to `SettingsStore` and `SettingsPanel`, so the GDD's verbosity toggle persists across games and sessions instead of being a game-local `extraToggles` switch.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.2 verbosity and tooltips (the Full/Concise toggle).
- §3.6 B8.
- §3.4 accessibility: a shared, persistent reading-comfort preference.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` persists the end-turn keybind (`tce-endturn-keybind`) and tooltips (`tce-show-tooltips`); reduced motion lives in `src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` (`tce-ui-reduced-motion`). There is no verbosity key or getter/setter.
- `SettingsPanel.extraToggles` (`src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`) provides a game-local toggle, but nothing shared or persisted by name.
- `getTooltips()` / `setTooltips()` show the shape a shared preference has; verbosity has no equivalent.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Extra-small** (half a day or less): the nearest precedent is the tooltips toggle pair in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` plus the `extraToggles` wiring in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`.
- Band is extra-small because it is one storage key, one getter/setter pair and one panel toggle, mirroring an existing one.

## Proposed shape

- `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity('full' | 'concise')` with a storage key and a safe fallback when storage is unavailable (mirror `getTooltips`).
- A first-class panel toggle rather than an `extraToggles` entry.
- Unit tests: default when unset, round-trip, unavailable storage, panel reflects the stored value.

# Make game-asset and game-source sibling resolution worktree-aware

## Problem

When a build runs from a worktree directory (`.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`), sibling game path resolution (e.g. `../tce-main-street` from `configs/full.json`) resolves relative to the worktree root instead of the main checkout. This causes `planGameAssetLinks` (link-game-assets.ts) and `discoverGames` (vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts) to look at `.worklog/worktrees/tce-<game>` — another item's checkout or nothing — instead of the canonical `<main-checkout>/../tce-<game>`.

## Users

- Developer running `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` from a worktree.
- Audit/CI runs that invoke build from worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `planGameAssetLinks` (link-game-assets.ts) and `discoverGames` (vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts) resolve sibling paths relative to the main checkout when `projectRoot` is inside `.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`, using `<main-checkout>/../tce-<game>` instead of `<worktree>/../tce-<game>`.
- Non-worktree builds (running from the main checkout) behave identically to today.
- A unit test pins the worktree-inside sibling resolution case in `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` or `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`.
- `npm run build` and the unit suite stay green.

## Impact

A developer running a full-preset build from a worktree sees the correct game assets instead of silently picking up another item's checkout or missing assets entirely.

## Constraints

- The fix must not affect non-worktree builds (the common case).
- The fix must not change the composition/pruning logic in link-game-assets.ts — only the path resolution anchor.

## Existing state

- `vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`: `discoverGames()` resolves `entry.path` via `path.resolve(projectRoot, entry.path)`.
- `link-game-assets.ts`: `planGameAssetLinks()` resolves game paths via `path.resolve(options.projectRoot, game.path)`.
- `vite-game-assets-plugin.ts`: passes `projectRoot` from Vite's config root (which is the worktree dir when run from inside `.worklog/worktrees/<id>/`).
- Dangling link pruning (CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI) already handles the *symptom* (prunes stale links) but not the *root cause* (wrong resolution anchor).
- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` has a worktree-style layout test but uses `tce-golf` as a sibling path (not the canonical `../tce-golf`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — `discoverGames()` resolves sibling paths; needs worktree-aware anchor.
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts` — `planGameAssetLinks()` resolves sibling paths; needs worktree-aware anchor.
- `vite.config.ts` — passes `__dirname` to plugins (main checkout anchor); may need to detect worktree context.
- `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts` — add worktree-inside sibling resolution test.

## Related Work

- `CG-0MWTSRRWU0062OMI` — Composed-asset symlink composition is worktree-fragile (dangling link fails vite build). Fixes the build failure symptom; this item addresses the resolution root cause.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope:** Both asset resolution (`planGameAssetLinks`) and game-source resolution (`discoverGames`) share the same sibling-path resolution pattern and must be fixed together.
- **Assumption:** A worktree directory is identifiable by walking up from `projectRoot` to find the first parent that contains both `.worklog/` and `configs/` (i.e. the main checkout).
- **Risk:** A distribution checkout that happens to have a `.worklog/` directory at an unexpected level could be misdetected. Mitigation: require the main-checkout ancestor to also have `configs/<preset>.json` for the active preset.
- **Risk:** Existing tests (e.g. the worktree-style layout test in `link-game-assets.test.ts`) use `tce-golf` as a sibling path, not `../tce-golf`; the new test must use the canonical sibling path to be meaningful.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions — the existing description and repo context are sufficient.

## Summary

Add the scene-space enumeration core: a pure, Phaser-free module that walks the runtime's own
scene/beat/close/routing transitions over the **manifest + its content**, recording every scene
exit and every beat refusal inside the existing depth/state bounds.

This is the engine seam both invariants read; it must reproduce the runtime's decisions, not a
second copy of them.

## Context

- The parent's "Proposed shape" fixes the state tuple: `(scene, beat, clock remaining, resources,
  outcome rules applied)`, enumerated with the existing `maxDepth` / `maxStates` bounds, a bound
  hit staying a failure.
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` already carries the bounded-DFS, state-key and truncation
  reporting machinery to mirror; `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` already exports the pure
  decision helpers the runtime uses (`evaluateSceneCondition`, `classifySceneOutcome`,
  `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`).
- The clock is **not** a declared resource, which is exactly why this enumeration needs its own
  module: the CSV guard cannot see it.

## Scope

**In:** the enumeration model, its state key and bound handling, its report shape (explored
states, scene exits, refusals, truncation), and a parity test against the real runner.

**Out:** the two invariants (their own children), the CLI mode, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` exports `enumerateSceneSpace(manifest, cards, options)`
  returning a frozen report with: every explored state key, every observed scene exit (scene id,
  winning outcome rule id, outcome, clock remaining at close, whether the close was refusal-
  triggered) and every observed beat refusal (scene id, beat card id, clock cost, clock remaining).
- Transition decisions delegate to the runtime's pure helpers — outcome and route precedence are
  never re-derived: `evaluateSceneCondition`, `classifySceneOutcome`, `selectRoute`,
  `resolveRouteTarget` from `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts`, and `isOptionAffordable` from
  `src/story-line/compile.ts`.
- A parity test drives a real `createEpisodeRunner` over the clean control fixture (headless
  adapter double) along its authored routes and asserts the enumeration records the **same** scene
  exits (scene, rule id, outcome, refusal flag) for those routes.
- Bounds: `maxDepth` (beats per route) and `maxStates` (explored states) default to the CSV guard's
  values; a bound hit is reported as truncation and makes the report invalid — never a silent pass.
- Determinism: two enumerations of the same inputs produce byte-identical JSON (no clock, RNG or
  ambient state is read; state-key ordering and the JSON key order are fixed).
- Resource arithmetic mirrors today's engine exactly (unclamped, unbounded `applyResourceDelta`);
  the module comment records that the G4 clamping work (`CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`) is what will later
  change the arithmetic, and a unit test pins the current unclamped behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Model the content once (`cardsById`, compiled options, declared keys, start bag, bounds) and
  reuse it for every branch of the DFS, as `guard.ts` does.
- Represent a state by `(sceneId, beatId, clockRemaining, pendingChain, resource bag)`; apply an
  option's cost/extra effect with the same ordering the choice model uses and stop at an ending.
- Record refusals at the entry step (cost > remaining) as the close trigger and continue into the
  close + routing step, so the refusal's continuation is part of the same enumeration.
- Emit `sceneGuardToJson(report)` and `formatSceneGuardReport(report)` beside the existing guard
  serialisers, in the same style.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (new)
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` (read/pattern reference — bounds, state key, reporting)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (pure helpers: `evaluateSceneCondition`,
  `classifySceneOutcome`, `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` / `src/story-line/types.ts` (`EpisodeManifest`, `Scene`,
  `Beat`, `SceneOutcome`)
- `src/story-line/compile.ts` (`isOptionAffordable`, option model)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-fixtures.ts` (the lane from the previous child)

## Dependencies

Depends on the test-lane child (fixtures + helper).

## Deliverables

The enumeration module, its JSON/format serialisers, and a unit suite including the runner parity
proof, bound/truncation proof, determinism proof and unclamped-arithmetic pin.

## Summary

Assert the parent's first invariant — **no exhausted close classifies as `success`** — over the
enumerated scene space, and report a violation per offending scene exit.

A scene that runs out of clock is a failure by design (GDD §2.10 T3); content that silently
labels it a success truncates the player's run without telling them.

## Context

- The clock is not a declared resource, so the CSV guard cannot see this at all; only the
  scene-space enumeration (previous child) carries `budgetExhausted` into the outcome rules.
- `classifySceneOutcome` already exposes the winning `ruleId`, which makes the report precise:
  the violation names the rule that mislabelled the close, not just the scene.

## Scope

**In:** the invariant predicate, its violation record and report entry, and its tests.

**Out:** the refusal-stranding invariant (its own child), CLI exposure, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `enumerateSceneSpace` (or a companion `evaluateSceneSpaceGuard`) reports an invariant named
  `no-success-on-exhausted-close`, with `checked` and `violations` counts in the same shape the
  CSV guard's `gated-branch-survivable` uses.
- A scene exit whose close was refusal-triggered and whose winning rule classified `success`
  produces exactly one violation naming: scene id, refused beat card id, winning `ruleId`, and the
  classified outcome.
- The `exhausted-success` control fixture fails this invariant and **only** this invariant, with
  the violation naming the fixture's recorded scene id and rule id (no incidental second
  violation).
- False-positive controls: an exhausted close that classifies `partial` or `failure` is not
  flagged, and a scene with no refusal contributes no violations.
- The `clean` control fixture passes, and a scene whose `success` close follows a **paid** beat
  (not a refusal) is not flagged.

- Derive the predicate from the enumeration's scene-exit records (the refusal flag is already on
  the record), so no second traversal is added.
- Add the violation record to the report's `violations` array in the existing guard JSON shape.
- Tests are table-driven over the control fixtures plus an inline minimal manifest for the
  false-positive cases.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (the invariant predicate + violation record)
- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` (read only — `ContentGuardInvariant` / violation shape)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (extend)

The invariant, its violation reporting, the passing/failing fixture assertions, and the
false-positive controls.

## Summary

Assert the parent's second invariant — **no refusal leads to a state with no reachable ending** —
so a refused beat can never strand the player in a dead scene.

This is GDD §2.8.6 item 5 and §2.10 T3: the refusal is a failure *with* authored recovery content,
never a silent truncation.

## Context

- The refusal closes the scene (`budgetExhausted`), and the close routes through the authored
  route table; a route may loop, terminate in a non-ending beat, or reach an ending.
- The check needs its own bounded search from each refusal state; the enumeration's explored
  states and the existing bounds are the machinery to reuse.

## Scope

**In:** the reachability predicate from a refusal state to a declared ending, its violation record
and report entry, and its tests.

**Out:** the exhausted-success invariant, CLI exposure, documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guard reports an invariant named `refusal-reaches-ending` with `checked` and `violations`
  counts, in the existing report shape.
- A refusal from which no continuation reaches any `manifest.endings` entry produces exactly one
  violation naming the scene id, the refused beat card id, the route taken on the exhausted close,
  and the terminal states the search reached instead of an ending.
- The `refusal-strand` control fixture fails this invariant and only this invariant, naming the
  fixture's recorded scene and refused beat.
- Recovery controls pass: a refusal whose exhausted-close route reaches a failure scene and then an
  ending (the GDD's `le-iii-approach` shape) is not flagged.
- A bound hit during the reachability search is reported as truncation and fails closed (never a
  pass); cycles that revisit a state terminate through the state key, so a reset ending is an
  ordinary passing shape.

## Minimal implementation

- Start the search from the exhausted close's selected route resolution (reusing
  `selectRoute` / `resolveRouteTarget`), then reuse the enumeration's successor expansion and
  state key.
- Share the bound accounting with the enumeration (one truncation report), so two invariants can
  never disagree about whether the space was fully explored.
- Tests are table-driven over the control fixtures plus an inline loop fixture.

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts` (reachability predicate + violation record)
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (read only — `selectRoute`, `resolveRouteTarget`)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard.test.ts` (extend)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-fixtures.ts` (control fixtures + intended-violation data)

## Dependencies

Depends on the enumeration child. Independent of the exhausted-success invariant.

## Deliverables

The invariant, its violation reporting, the failing fixture assertion, the recovery control and the
loop/truncation proofs.

## Summary

Add the irreversible declaration seam: thread `irreversible` through the projection, content adapter, and episode runner so the engine knows which keys can never be granted back.

## Description

The engine currently has no notion of irreversible resource keys. This child establishes the declarative foundation so that subsequent children can refuse grants on irreversible keys.

**Key design decisions:**

- **Runtime declaration:** Extend `createResourceProjection` with an `{ irreversible }` option on the projection. The `StorylineResourceProjection` interface gains an `irreversible: readonly StorylineResourceKey[]` member. This mirrors how the declared set is already carried.
- **Authoring declaration:** Add `irreversibleResources?: readonly string[]` to `ContentAdapter`. The `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` script reads this and passes it to `validateContentCsv` → `validateStorylineOptions`.
- **Single-source wiring:** The episode runner reads `manifest.resources.irreversible` (already delivered by G2) and threads it into both the projection option and the content adapter validation. The manifest is the authoritative source.
- **No new adapter member:** The projection carries the declaration, so no parallel seam is needed.

**AC alignment:**
- AC7 (single-source declaration) is satisfied by deriving from the manifest.
- AC3 (resolution-time guard) can wire through the projection's `irreversible` member.
- AC1 (authoring-time validation) can read from the content adapter.

**Key files:**
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — `createResourceProjection` option; `irreversible` on `StorylineResourceProjection`.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — `ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources?`.
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — `LONG_ERASURE_CONTENT_ADAPTER.irreversibleResources: ['hull']`.
- `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` — thread manifest's `irreversible` into projection creation.

**Tests:**
- `tests/story-line/irreversible-declaration.test.ts` — unit tests for `createResourceProjection({ irreversible: [...] })` carrying the set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createResourceProjection(fields, { irreversible: ['hull'] })` returns a projection whose `irreversible` member is exactly `['hull']` (declaration order preserved).
- A `createResourceProjection(fields)` call with no option returns `irreversible: []` — the default declares nothing, so behaviour is unchanged.
- `ContentAdapter` accepts an optional `irreversibleResources: readonly string[]` and `LONG_ERASURE_CONTENT_ADAPTER` declares `['hull']`.
- The episode runner threads `manifest.resources.irreversible` into the projection so a manifest-declared key reaches the engine seam (unit test asserts the projection sees it).
- With no irreversible key declared, every existing story-line unit suite stays green without edits.
- A unit test asserts the projection's `irreversible` member is carried and defaults to empty (`tests/story-line/irreversible-declaration.test.ts`).
- One authoritative declaration: the manifest's `resources.irreversible`, the content-adapter declaration and the engine projection cannot drift silently — either the wiring is derived from a single source or a mismatch is reported, and a unit test asserts that a divergence between the adapter declaration and the projection set is surfaced rather than silently accepted.

## Impact

A designer can declare a resource key irreversible once and the engine carries that declaration into the run, so the hull dial's no-refund promise rests on an engine seam instead of authoring habit.

## Summary

At resolution time, refuse a positive `#extra` grant on a declared irreversible key — the key is not applied, and the refusal is logged once in the activity log naming the key, while the rest of the option still resolves.

## Description

This guard is the runtime enforcement complement to the authoring-time rule (CG-0MWUQQAEW0078270). It must not change the arithmetic in `applyResourceDelta`; the refusal happens upstream at delta selection, as documented in the parent's constraints.

**Implementation approach:**

1. **`selectDeclaredDelta` in `resources.ts`** — extend the function (or create a companion `selectDeclaredNonIrreversibleDelta`) to accept an `irreversible` set and filter positive-grant keys from it. The function already separates `delta` (declared) from `ignored` (undeclared). Add a new `refused: StorylineResourceKey[]` bucket for irreversible-grant refusals.
2. **`applyDeclaredDelta` in `resolve.ts`** — when the `extraEffect` path (sign `+1`) encounters a key in `refused`, log `Extra effect refused: <key> is irreversible.` (using the existing activity-log shape) and omit it from the delta. Cost deductions (sign `-1`) are never refused — irreversible keys may be spent.
3. **Reuse the existing `ignored` channel shape** — the activity-log line follows the same pattern: `Extra effect refused: hull is irreversible.` rather than inventing a new member.
4. **The projection's `irreversible` member** — `resolveStorylineOption` already reads `adapter.resources` and passes it to `applyDeclaredDelta`. The irreversible set from the projection is threaded through.

**Key files:**
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — `selectDeclaredDelta` gains `{ irreversible }` parameter; returns `{ delta, ignored, refused }`.
- `src/story-line/resolve.ts` — `applyDeclaredDelta` accepts `irreversible` set; logs refusal for extraEffect grants on irreversible keys.
- `src/story-line/index.ts` — thread projection's `irreversible` into `resolveStorylineOption` → `applyDeclaredDelta`.

**Tests:**
- `tests/story-line/resource-semantics.test.ts` — `selectDeclaredDelta` with irreversible set: positive key refused, negative key passed, non-irreversible key passed.
- `tests/story-line/irreversible-policy.test.ts` — end-to-end resolution: option with `#extra=hull:1` logs refusal, state unchanged.


## Acceptance Criteria

- `selectDeclaredDelta(source, +1, declared, { irreversible })` moves a positive-grant key present in `irreversible` into a `refused` list instead of the delta — the key is never applied.
- The same key with a negative sign (a `#cost=hull:1` deduction) is **not** refused: an irreversible key may be spent, never granted.
- `resolveStorylineOption` with `#extra=hull:1` on a hull-irreversible projection refuses the grant: `state` hull is unchanged, the activity log gains **one** line naming the key (`Extra effect refused: hull is irreversible.`), and the rest of the option (cost, effect, successor push) still resolves.
- The refusal uses the existing activity-log channel shape — no new adapter member is required.
- With no irreversible declaration, `selectDeclaredDelta` behaviour is byte-identical to today (all declared deltas forwarded, `refused` empty).
- Unit tests cover the refusal at both `selectDeclaredDelta` level and end-to-end resolution (`tests/story-line/resource-semantics.test.ts`, `tests/story-line/irreversible-policy.test.ts`).

## Impact

A grant to a declared never-restored resource is visibly refused in play instead of silently refilling the dial, so a hull point lost during a run can never be handed back by a mistyped option.

## Summary

Add a validation rule that refuses a positive `#extra` on a declared irreversible key at authoring time, reported as a hard `ContentIssue` with code `irreversible-grant`, naming the card id, CSV row, options column, and offending key.

## Description

This is the authoring-time gate. When `validateStorylineOptions` receives an `extraEffect` entry whose key is in the irreversible set, it reports a hard issue rather than a warning. The CSV content validator (`validateContentCsv`) passes the irreversible set from the adapter.

**Implementation approach:**

1. **New validation code** — add `'irreversible-grant'` to `StorylineValidationCode` in `src/story-line/validate.ts`. When present, `validateStorylineOptions` checks every `extraEffect.<key>` value > 0 against the irreversible set.
2. **`ValidateStorylineOptionsOptions` extension** — add `{ irreversible?: Iterable<StorylineContentKey> }` to the config interface. When supplied, positive `extraEffect` on any of those keys is rejected.
3. **`ContentIssueCode` extension** — add `'irreversible-grant'` to `ContentIssueCode` in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts`. The `reason` field carries `'irreversible-grant'` from the underlying `StorylineValidationIssue.code`.
4. **Content adapter plumbing** — `validateContentCsv` reads `adapter.irreversibleResources` (from Child 1) and passes `{ irreversible: adapter.irreversibleResources }` to `validateStorylineOptions`.
5. **`scripts/validate-storylines.ts`** — the script passes the adapter's `irreversibleResources` through to `validateContentCsv`.

**Key files:**
- `src/story-line/validate.ts` — `'irreversible-grant'` in `StorylineValidationCode`; check in the `extraEffect` loop.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — `'irreversible-grant'` in `ContentIssueCode`; thread `irreversible` from adapter to `validateStorylineOptions`.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — `ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources?` (from Child 1).
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — no change needed if the adapter is already read (it is).

**Tests:**
- `tests/story-line/validate.test.ts` — `validateStorylineOptions` with `irreversible: ['hull']` and `extraEffect: { hull: 1 }` → `irreversible-grant` issue.
- `tests/story-line/content/gdd-resource-model.test.ts` — a fixture CSV row granting `hull` via `#extra` → hard issue with stable code.
- End-to-end: `npm run storylines:validate` fails with `irreversible-grant` on a violating row.

**Depends on:** CG-0MWUQQAEW0078270 (declaration seam: `ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources?`).


## Acceptance Criteria

- `validateStorylineOptions` with `irreversible: ['hull']` and an option `extraEffect: { hull: 1 }` reports a hard issue with `code: 'irreversible-grant'`, naming the key in `message` and `resource`.
- A non-positive `extraEffect` on an irreversible key is **not** reported by this rule (`#extra` is a gain by definition; `#cost=hull:1` still validates).
- `validateContent` / `validateContentCsv` surfaces the issue as a hard `ContentIssue` whose `code` is `'irreversible-grant'` (or a `reason` under an existing code) and whose fields include the card id, the 1-based CSV `row`, the `options` column, and the offending key.
- `npm run storylines:validate` exits non-zero on a CSV row granting a declared irreversible key, naming the row and key in its output.
- A fixture CSV row that grants a declared irreversible key exists, and a unit test asserts the diagnostic end-to-end including the reported row and column.
- With **no** irreversible key declared (the default `coins`/`reputation` pair), validation output is byte-identical to today — no new issues on existing fixtures.
- `ContentAdapter.irreversibleResources` (from the declaration seam) is the authoring declaration source; no new CLI flag is required for the shipped adapters.


## Impact

Authors who try to refill a never-restored resource (such as the Long Erasure's hull) now get a precise row-and-column authoring error instead of a silent runtime refusal.
